UNITS.tt: ekmek var mı? · is there any bread?

lines: [i]Merhaba[/i] = hello · [i]Günaydın[/i] = good morning · [i]İyi günler[/i] = good day
Leaving: [i]Hoşça kal[/i] (you stay) · [i]Güle güle[/i] (said to the one leaving) · [i]Görüşürüz[/i] = see you
Polite address: [b]efendim[/b]. Shopkeeper greets you: [i]Buyurun![/i] = "go ahead / how can I help".

qs.q: You are LEAVING a shop. The shopkeeper says?
qs.x: güle güle is said TO the leaver

ls.t: var / yok — There is, there isn't
lines: Turkish has no verb "to have" here. It uses [b]var[/b] (exists) and [b]yok[/b] (doesn't exist).
[i]Ekmek [b]var[/b].[/i] = There is bread. · [i]Ekmek [b]yok[/b].[/i] = There is no bread.
Ask by adding mı: [i]Ekmek var [b]mı[/b]?[/i] = Is there any bread?

qs.q: The café is out of tea. They say:

lines: [b]mi/mı/mu/mü[/b] is a separate little word that turns any statement into a question.
It harmonizes with the last vowel: güzel→[b]mi[/b] · var→[b]mı[/b] · yorgun→[b]mu[/b] · Türk→[b]mü[/b]
[i]Bu güzel mi?[/i] = Is this beautiful? — Turkish never changes word order for questions. 🎯

qs.q: Which is TRUE about Turkish questions?

lines: Turkish has no separate verb "to be" — it glues endings on: [i]Türk[b]üm[/b][/i] = I am Turkish.
-im (I) · -sin (you) · —(he/she/it, nothing!) · -iz (we) · -siniz (you plural/polite) · -ler (they)
[i]Öğrenci[b]yim[/b][/i] = I am a student. (y is a buffer after a vowel) 🔤
[i]Nerelisiniz?[/i] = Where are you from? Answer with [b]-li[/b]: [i]Amerikalı[b]yım[/b][/i] = I'm American.
[i]İstanbullu[/i] = from Istanbul · [i]Sacramentolu[/i] = from Sacramento 😎
Politely: [i]Adınız ne?[/i] = What is your name? · [i]Memnun oldum[/i] = Pleased to meet you.
1 bir · 2 iki · 3 üç · 4 dört · 5 beş · 6 altı · 7 yedi · 8 sekiz · 9 dokuz · 10 on
Then just stack: 11 [b]on bir[/b] · 12 [b]on iki[/b] · 20 [b]yirmi[/b] · 21 [b]yirmi bir[/b]
Remember: after a number the noun stays SINGULAR — [i]beş kokteyl[/i], never "beş kokteyller" 🍹

UNITS.tt: daha koymayın, lütfen! · no more, please!

lines: [i]Bir çay lütfen[/i] = one tea please · [i]Ne tavsiye edersiniz?[/i] = what do you recommend?
[i]Hesap lütfen[/i] = the bill please · [i]Afiyet olsun![/i] = enjoy your meal!
Reply to thanks: [i]Bir şey değil[/i] = it's nothing / you're welcome.

qs.q: You finished eating and want to pay:

lines: The bare verb stem IS the command: [i]gel![/i] = come! · [i]bak![/i] = look! · [i]dur![/i] = stop!
Polite plural: add [b]-in/-ın/-un/-ün[/b]: [i]gel[b]in[/b][/i] = please come · [i]bak[b]ın[/b][/i] = look
Negative command: [b]-me/-ma[/b]: [i]gitme![/i] = don't go! · [i]koyma![/i] = don't put!
[i]sağa[/i] = to the right · [i]sola[/i] = to the left · [i]düz[/i] = straight
[i]Sağa dönün[/i] = turn right · [i]Düz gidin[/i] = go straight on
[i]ileride[/i] = up ahead · [i]burada[/i] = here · [i]orada[/i] = there 📍
Verb stem + [b]-iyor[/b] + person = the "-ing" tense. [i]Gel[b]iyorum[/b][/i] = I am coming.
It also covers routines: [i]Her sabah kahve iç[b]iyorum[/b][/i] = I drink coffee every morning ☕
Watch the softening: git → [i]gid[b]iyor[/b][/i], et → [i]ed[b]iyor[/b][/i] (t becomes d).
Slip [b]-mi/-mı/-mu/-mü[/b] in before -yor: [i]gel[b]mi[/b]yorum[/i] = I am not coming.
[i]Sigara iç[b]mi[/b]yorum[/i] = I don't smoke 🚭 (a very useful sentence!)
Question + negative: [i]Gelmiyor musun?[/i] = Aren't you coming?
[b]benim[/b] ...-im = my · [b]senin[/b] ...-in = your · [b]onun[/b] ...-i = his/her
[i]benim köpeğ[b]im[/b][/i] = my dog (k softens to ğ!) · [i]senin araba[b]n[/b][/i] = your car
To say "I have": [i]Bir köpeğim [b]var[/b][/i] = I have a dog. Literally "my dog exists" 🐶

UNITS.tt: çok beklediniz mi? · have you been waiting long?

lines: Stem + [b]-di/-dı/-du/-dü[/b] + person. [i]Gel[b]dim[/b][/i] = I came. [i]Git[b]ti[/b][/i] = he went.
After hard consonants (p,ç,t,k,s,ş,h,f) it hardens to [b]-ti[/b]: [i]iç[b]ti[/b]m[/i] = I drank.
Negative: [i]gel[b]me[/b]dim[/i] = I didn't come.
[i]Saat kaç?[/i] = What time is it? · [i]Saat üç[/i] = It's 3 o'clock.
[i]üç buçuk[/i] = half past three · [i]üçe çeyrek var[/i] = quarter TO three
[i]üçü çeyrek geçiyor[/i] = quarter PAST three ⏰
[i]Tanıştırayım[/i] = let me introduce · [i]Bu benim arkadaşım[/i] = this is my friend
[i]Bu benim erkek arkadaşım Kaan[/i] = this is my boyfriend Kaan ❤
[i]Memnun oldum[/i] = pleased to meet you · reply: [i]Ben de[/i] = me too.

UNITS.tt: yarın erken kalkacağım · I'll get up early tomorrow

lines: Stem + [b]-ecek/-acak[/b] + person: [i]gid[b]eceğim[/b][/i] = I will go.
[i]Yarın erken kalk[b]acağım[/b][/i] = tomorrow I will get up early ⏰ (Trader Joe's line!)
Negative: [i]git[b]me[/b]yeceğim[/i] = I won't go.
[b]-elim/-alım[/b] = let's ... : [i]Gid[b]elim[/b]![/i] = let's go! · [i]Bak[b]alım[/b][/i] = let's see
[i]Hadi bakalım![/i] = come on then! (your battle cry 🗣️)
Ask permission: [i]Gideyim mi?[/i] = shall I go?
[i]üstünde[/i] = on top of · [i]altında[/i] = under · [i]içinde[/i] = inside · [i]yanında[/i] = next to
[i]arkasında[/i] = behind · [i]önünde[/i] = in front of · [i]arasında[/i] = between
[i]Köpek masanın [b]altında[/b][/i] = the dog is under the table 🐶

UNITS.tt: yardım eder misiniz? · would you help me?

lines: [b]-er misiniz?[/b] = would you...? [i]Yardım eder misiniz?[/i] = would you help me?
[i]Açar mısınız?[/i] = would you open it? · [i]Söyler misiniz?[/i] = would you tell me?
Softest of all: [i]...rica ediyorum[/i] = I request... 🎩
[b]-mek istemek[/b] = to want to: [i]Gitmek [b]istiyorum[/b][/i] = I want to go.
[i]Türkçe öğrenmek istiyorum[/i] = I want to learn Turkish 🇹🇷
Negative: [i]Gitmek istemiyorum[/i] = I don't want to go.
Glue events with: [i]sonra[/i] = then · [i]ondan sonra[/i] = after that · [i]birden[/i] = suddenly
[i]önce[/i] = first/before · [i]en sonunda[/i] = finally · [i]bir gün[/i] = one day
[i]Bir gün plaja gittim, sonra bir kokteyl içtim.[/i] 🍹

UNITS.tt: nereye gidelim? · where shall we go?

lines: Stem + [b]-ebil/-abil[/b] = can: [i]Yap[b]abil[/b]irim[/i] = I can do it.
[i]Türkçe konuş[b]abil[/b]iyorum[/i] = I can speak Turkish 🗣️
Cannot: special form [b]-emem/-amam[/b]: [i]Gid[b]emem[/b][/i] = I can't go.
[b]daha[/b] = more: [i]daha büyük[/i] = bigger · [b]en[/b] = most: [i]en güzel[/i] = the most beautiful
Than = [b]-den/-dan[/b]: [i]Benden daha hızlı[/i] = faster than me 🏃‍♀️
[i]Bandit dünyanın [b]en[/b] tatlı köpeği![/i] = Bandit is the world's cutest dog 🐶
[i]Ne kadar güzel![/i] = How beautiful! · [i]Ne güzel bir gün![/i] = What a lovely day!
[i]Aman Allahım![/i] = Oh my God! · [i]Vallahi![/i] = I swear! · [i]Allah Allah![/i] = well I never!
[i]Maşallah![/i] = wonderful (said to protect from the evil eye) 🧿

o: praise & ward off the evil eye

UNITS.tt: neler yapmayı seviyorsunuz? · what do you like doing?

lines: Stem + [b]-meli/-malı[/b] + person = must/should: [i]Git[b]meli[/b]yim[/i] = I must go.
[i]Erken kalk[b]malı[/b]yım[/i] = I must get up early ⏰
Also: [i]...-mem lazım[/i] = I need to: [i]Gitmem lazım[/i] = I gotta go.
[b]sevmek[/b] = to love/like: [i]Denizi seviyorum[/i] = I love the sea 🌊
Liking an ACTION: [b]-meyi sevmek[/b]: [i]Dans etmeyi seviyorum[/i] = I love dancing 💃
[i]hoşlanmak[/i] = to be fond of · [i]nefret etmek[/i] = to hate
[i]Bence[/i] = in my opinion · [i]...-sen iyi olur[/i] = it'd be good if you...
[i]Dinlenmelisin[/i] = you should rest · [i]Doktora git[/i] = go to the doctor 👩‍⚕️
[i]Geçmiş olsun[/i] = get well soon (also said after any bad experience!)

qs.q: A friend is sick. You say:

UNITS.tt: eğer geçmezse, ilaç veririm · if it doesn't get better...

lines: [b]-se/-sa[/b] = if: [i]Gel[b]ir[/b]sen[/i] = if you come · [i]İster[b]sen[/b][/i] = if you want
[i][b]Eğer[/b] yağmur yağarsa, plaja gitmeyiz[/i] = if it rains, we won't go to the beach 🌧️
[b]eğer[/b] is optional — the -se ending already means "if".
[i]...-e ihtiyacım var[/i] = I need...: [i]Para[b]ya[/b] ihtiyacım var[/i] = I need money 💵
[i]Yardıma ihtiyacım var[/i] = I need help · [i]Bir doktora ihtiyacım var[/i]
Quick version: [i]Su lazım[/i] = (I) need water.
[i]İki yıl[b]dır[/b] burada yaşıyorum[/i] = I've been living here for two years.
Turkish uses the PRESENT tense with -dır for ongoing time — not the past! 🕰️
[i]Ne kadar zamandır?[/i] = for how long?

qs.q: "I have been waiting for an hour" uses which tense in Turkish?

UNITS.tt: sizce çok sakin bir yermiş! · you said it was quiet!

lines: [i]Şikayet etmek istiyorum[/i] = I want to complain · [i]Bu kabul edilemez[/i] = this is unacceptable
[i]Özür dilerim[/i] = I apologize · [i]Affedersiniz[/i] = excuse me · [i]Pardon[/i] = sorry
[i]Kusura bakmayın[/i] = please don't take offence 🙇‍♀️

qs.q: You bump into someone. You say:

lines: [b]...-diğini söyledi[/b] = said that...: [i]Geleceğ[b]ini[/b] söyledi[/i] = he said he would come.
[i]Josh uzaylı gördüğ[b]ünü[/b] söyledi[/i] = Josh said he saw an alien 👽
Turkish packs the whole clause into a noun-like chunk before the main verb.
Turkish softens complaints with fixed phrases. [i]Kusura bakmayın[/i] = please overlook my fault.
[i]Rica ederim[/i] = you're welcome / I request it · [i]Estağfurullah[/i] = not at all, don't mention it
To a person working: [i]Kolay gelsin[/i] = may it come easy. Turks say this constantly. 💪

UNITS.tt: aradığınız numara yanlıştır · the number is incorrect

lines: [b]-en/-an[/b] = the one who does: [i]dans [b]eden[/b] kız[/i] = the girl who dances 💃
[b]-diği[/b] = the thing that someone does: [i]ara[b]dığınız[/b] numara[/i] = the number you dialled
Turkish puts the whole description BEFORE the noun. English goes after. 🔄
[b]-ip[/b] chains two verbs by the same person: [i]Gid[b]ip[/b] aldım[/i] = I went and bought it.
Only the LAST verb carries the tense and person. Efficient! ⚡
[i]Kalkıp dans etti[/i] = she got up and danced.
Announcements use [b]-dir[/b] to sound formal: [i]Yanlıştır[/i] = it IS incorrect.
[i]Aradığınız numara yanlıştır[/i] = the number you have dialled is incorrect ☎️
[i]Kapanmıştır[/i] = it has closed · [i]Yasaktır[/i] = it is forbidden 🚫

UNITS.tt: ne olduğunu anlatır mısınız? · could you tell me what happened?

lines: [b]-iyordu[/b] = was ...ing: [i]Dans ed[b]iyordu[/b][/i] = she was dancing.
[i]Yürüyordum ve birden bir hayalet gördüm![/i] = I was walking and suddenly saw a ghost 👻
Use it for the BACKGROUND, and -di for the sudden event.

qs.q: For a sudden completed event you use:

lines: [b]-miş[/b] = apparently / I heard / so they say. Turkish MARKS second-hand info! 🤯
[i]Gel[b]miş[/b][/i] = apparently he came (I didn't see it myself).
[i]Çok sakin bir yer[b]miş[/b]![/i] = they said it was a very quiet place!

qs.q: You did NOT witness it yourself. Use:

lines: Three pasts, three jobs: [b]-di[/b] I saw it · [b]-iyordu[/b] it was ongoing · [b]-miş[/b] I heard it
[i]Geldi[/i] (he came, I know) vs [i]gelmiş[/i] (he came, apparently) vs [i]geliyordu[/i] (he was coming)
Pluperfect [b]-mişti[/b] = had already happened: [i]gitmişti[/i] = he had gone.

UNITS.tt: güldürme beni! · don't make me laugh!

lines: [b]-erdi/-ardı[/b] = used to: [i]Çocukken burada oyna[b]rdım[/b][/i] = I used to play here as a kid 🧒
Perfect for Livermore memories: [i]Bu evde otururduk[/i] = we used to live in this house 🏡
[i]-ken[/i] = while/when: [i]çocuk[b]ken[/b][/i] = when (I was) a child.
[b]-dir/-tir/-t[/b] makes a verb causative: [i]gül[/i] (laugh) → [i]gül[b]dür[/b][/i] (make laugh) 😂
[i]Güldürme beni![/i] = don't make me laugh! · [i]yap[/i] (do) → [i]yap[b]tır[/b][/i] (have it done)
[i]Saçımı kestir[b]dim[/b][/i] = I had my hair cut (someone else did it) ✂️
[i]Yok artık![/i] = no way! · [i]Ciddi misin?[/i] = are you serious? · [i]İnanmıyorum![/i] = I don't believe it!
[i]Hadi canım![/i] = oh come on! · [i]Vay be![/i] = wow!
Josh says aliens are real. You say: [i]Yok artık Josh![/i] 👽

UNITS.tt: burası ne zaman inşa edilmiş? · when was this built?

lines: Add [b]-il/-in[/b] to make the passive: [i]yap[/i] (build) → [i]yap[b]ıl[/b]dı[/i] = it was built.
[i]Burası ne zaman inşa edil[b]miş[/b]?[/i] = when was this place built? 🏛️
The doer, if mentioned, takes [b]tarafından[/b]: [i]Kaan tarafından yapıldı[/i].
[b]-ci/-cı[/b] = the person who does it: [i]kahve[/i] → [i]kahve[b]ci[/b][/i] = coffee seller ☕
[i]iş[/i] (work) → [i]iş[b]çi[/b][/i] = worker · [i]gazete[/i] → [i]gazete[b]ci[/b][/i] = journalist
[b]-lik[/b] = the abstract thing: [i]güzel[/i] → [i]güzel[b]lik[/b][/i] = beauty ✨
[b]-ci[/b] maker/seller · [b]-lik[/b] abstract noun · [b]-siz[/b] without · [b]-li[/b] with/from
[i]şeker[b]siz[/b][/i] = without sugar (essential for coffee!) ☕ · [i]süt[b]lü[/b][/i] = with milk
[i]Türkçe[/i] itself = Türk + çe, the "in the manner of" ending. 🇹🇷

UNITS.tt: fiyatları bilseydim orada yemezdik · if I had known...

lines: [b]-seydi[/b] = if (only) ... had: [i]Bil[b]seydim[/b][/i] = if I had known.
[i]Fiyatları bilseydim orada yemezdik[/i] = if I'd known the prices we wouldn't have eaten there 💸
The result clause takes [b]-ezdi[/b]: [i]gitmezdim[/i] = I wouldn't have gone.
[b]Keşke[/b] = if only: [i]Keşke gelseydin[/i] = if only you had come 🥺
[i]Keşke Türkçe öğrenseydim[/i] = if only I had learned Turkish... (but you ARE! 🎉)
And the sweetest sentence in this whole book: [i]Seni seviyorum.[/i] ❤
You have covered the entire book: greetings, tenses, cases, conditionals, reported speech.
Turkish is agglutinative — you now know the game: find the stem, stack the endings, respect the vowels.
Kaan is going to lose his mind when you say: [i]Türkçe öğrendim, seni seviyorum.[/i] ❤
